{"id":"persona-qbnm.1","title":"gpg: sign the challenge with gpg-agent","description":"hire-attestors/src/gpg.rs enumerates keys by parsing 'gpg --with-colons' (:139-147) and applies the enrolment rule recorded in the gpg-key-validity-policy memory, but inherits the default prove() and so produces no evidence.

Closest sibling to ssh.rs, which is the model: connect to the agent, have it sign the daemon's challenge, verify the signature against both the challenge and the key the candidate names. gpg-agent speaks Assuan over its socket; the key never leaves the agent.

Assurance is iaa1 per SPEC-HIRE -- self-asserted, key custody assumed. Presence: decide deliberately. ssh.rs claims NONE and documents why (an agent key with no passphrase and no confirm flag signs without prompting anybody). gpg-agent is different: it often DOES prompt for a passphrase via pinentry, and a key cached in the agent does not. So the same key can prove with or without a human depending on cache state. That makes gpg the first source where proof cost (persona-jl4j.3) is DYNAMIC rather than static, which is worth getting right here rather than discovering later.

Do not claim presence from the mere fact that pinentry could have appeared.","acceptance_criteria":"A signature over the daemon's challenge, verified against the candidate's key; presence claimed only when a human actually authenticated; proof cost reported honestly given agent cache state.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-15T20:49:56.063831716Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-15T20:49:56.063831716Z","labels":["attestor","driver","crypto"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-qbnm.1","depends_on_id":"persona-qbnm","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-15T20:49:56.100482318Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"THIS IS THE PRIORITY PATH, Mark 2026-09-15: 'our best immediate proof is going to be a usb token like the ones used by the kernel dev team.' That is a Yubikey or Nitrokey holding the PGP key on its smartcard applet, driven through gpg-agent and scdaemon -- the kernel.org workflow for signing tags and releases. So this bead, not persona-qbnm.3, is the shortest path to a real hardware proof: fido2 needs a feature that is off by default and a new dependency, gpg-agent is already reachable and the enumeration already works.

THE SERIAL IS ALREADY PARSED AND THEN DISCARDED. hire-attestors/src/gpg.rs:96:

    let secret_held = fields.get(14).is_some_and(|f| *f != "#");

with the comment directly above naming exactly what is being thrown away: field 15 is '+' for a local secret key, '#' for a stub, and 'anything else a token serial number'. So the daemon ALREADY KNOWS a key is card-resident and collapses it to a boolean. Today a Yubikey-held key grades identically to one sitting in ~/.gnupg, which understates it badly. Keep the enrolment rule exactly as it is -- see the gpg-key-validity-policy memory, where smartcard serials counting as possession was a deliberate decision -- and stop discarding which kind of possession it was.

WHERE THE HARDWARE FACT GOES: into provenance, NOT into the tier. Do not touch IdentityAssurance for this. SPEC-HIRE defines Iaa3 as hardware-bound AND IdP-verified, and a self-asserted PGP key is not IdP-verified however good the card is, so Iaa1 stays correct -- Iaa1 means nobody vouched for who the operator is, which is true. What is currently unrecorded is that the key cannot be copied off the device, and that belongs in auth_methods alongside the source name. persona-5s4b.129 is the bead for that, and it is the cheap answer rather than a new assurance tier.

TOUCH POLICY IS REAL PRESENCE AND IS WORTH CHASING HERE. A Yubikey OpenPGP applet can be configured to require a physical touch per signature (the User Interaction Flag, visible in gpg --card-status). A signature from such a card IS a human touching hardware, which is PresenceLevel::Hardware honestly earned -- and it would make this bead the FIRST source in the tree to establish any presence at all, ahead of fido2.

That needs a HardwareTouch constructor. claim.rs's ponytail comment on that type already anticipates it: 'one constructor per authenticator family here -- CTAP2 and PKCS#11 slot 9A have different witnesses, so do not force one byte layout on both'. An OpenPGP card is a third family. Add it there, not in gpg.rs.

Note the honest combination this produces: Iaa1 with Hardware presence. Not a contradiction -- self-asserted identity, hardware-verified human. The two axes are separate and the model already reports them separately. Do not try to promote it to Iaa3; the fold at claim.rs correctly refuses, because no IdP vouched.","priority":1}

Implemented in 911f55e. gpg signs the daemon's challenge inline through gpg-agent; ChallengeSignature::verify_openpgp checks VALIDSIG, matches the candidate's fingerprint in either the signing or the primary position (the smartcard shape), and compares the data gpg says the signature covers against the challenge. Presence stays None and the tier stays Iaa1, as the bead required. The verifier is the locally installed gpg, asserted rather than replaced: in-process packet parsing would keep the dependence on the same binary's keyring for the public key, so it shrinks the trust set by nothing. Tests: hire-attestors/tests/gpg_agent_live.rs against real gpg with TWO keys in one keyring, so a good signature by the wrong key is caught -- a single-key keyring cannot make that assertion; plus VALIDSIG fixtures captured from GnuPG 2.4.4 including the certify-only-primary case. Both verification checks were mutation-tested and each fails the suite when broken. Verified end to end: hired issued a JWT-SVID with source=gpg for a named gpg identity.
